harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent daily log rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1. Seven compressed rotations are retained, and copytruncate allows an application holding the file open to continue writing. RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 remain unchanged. The configuration and log data survived a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, and copytruncate.
Validated the configuration with the installed RHEL-compatible logrotate 3.18.0.
Forced a rotation while a writer held app.log open; verified pre-rotation data in app.log.1.gz and subsequent output in app.log.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its boot ID changed, the system recovered, the logrotate timer remained active, and configuration and data persisted.

evidence.requirement: Rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily and retain seven compressed rotations
evidence.summary: The installed configuration contains daily, rotate 7, and compress; logrotate parses it as one-day rotation with seven rotations.

evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: A held-open writer emitted a pre-rotation marker, logrotate copied/truncated and compressed the file, then the same writer emitted a post-rotation marker into the active log. Both markers were verified in their expected files.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: Before and after work, node1 remained RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64; the existing RHEL logrotate 3.18.0 package was used.

Healthy baseline boot ID c2f29441-0515-4717-99f7-a7647824278d was captured, the safe reboot was acknowledged, and the recovered node reported changed boot ID 908613c4-98a9-4077-9d49-d2d00eefd2f2. Post-restart state was running with the logrotate timer enabled/active, policy and rotated data intact, and zero failed units.
